Acyclonucleosides are a class of antiviral drugs that have an open sugar ring structure, which differentiates them from other nucleoside analogs that typically have a closed sugar ring. Among the options provided, Ganciclovir is known to be an acyclonucleoside analog. Zidovudine, Ribavirin, and Lamivudine are nucleoside analogs but do not have the open structure characteristic of acyclonucleosides.
